source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

crude_exposure.evidence: Company commentary (FY26 earnings call context) notes Honasa's brands (Mamaearth, The Derma Co, Staze, Aqualogica) rely on raw materials/intermediates sourced from or routed through the Gulf region, and that beauty formulations and packaging are substantially derived from crude-oil derivatives, exposing input costs to crude price moves; no numeric % of raw material cost disclosed in sources found.

ABB.report_year: CY2024 (ABB India follows Jan-Dec fiscal year; Integrated Annual Report 2024)

china_plus_one.evidence: ABB India CEO commentary (Jan 2025, BusinessToday) described India as an 'export hub to support other geographies' and said he sees India becoming ABB's third-largest market; management also noted India contributes roughly 10-11% of ABB group's export market. No explicit 'China+1' framing or direct attribution of revenue/order growth to China+1 diversification was found in available sources.

govt_capex.evidence: Broker note (Motilal Oswal, Q4 CY2024 review) stated direct exposure to government customers is minimal, with indirect exposure through EPC contractors estimated at about 35-40% of business; order inflow growth for CY2024 (+6% YoY) was described as impacted by 'transient weakness from government and private capex'. CY2024 total orders were a record INR 13,079 crore and revenue INR 12,188 crore, with order backlog of INR 9,380 crore (+12% YoY).

inr_exposure.evidence: International business was ~54% of FY25 revenue (~INR 4,236 crore of total ~INR 7,896 crore), spanning Europe (~INR 1,474 crore, +4.4% YoY), Emerging Markets (~INR 1,510 crore, +27.9% YoY) and Canada/North America (~INR 1,252 crore, +35.7% YoY), implying material EUR/CAD and other non-INR currency exposure; no explicit hedging policy percentage disclosed in sources found. Domestic revenue was ~INR 3,660 crore (+16.4% YoY).

pli_scheme.evidence: Sources note Emcure commenced an API manufacturing facility at Kurkumbh, consistent with broader industry efforts (and a government PLI scheme for bulk drugs/APIs/KSMs exists), but no source confirmed Emcure as an approved PLI beneficiary or quantified any related revenue.

china_plus_one.evidence: Royal Enfield (Eicher Motors) reported exports up 29.7% to 100,136 units in FY25 (10.6% of total 1,002,893 units sold) and international business revenue of ~INR 2,546 crore (+38% YoY) against total FY25 revenue of ~INR 18,800 crore (+14.1% YoY). The company is diversifying its global manufacturing/assembly footprint via CKD operations in Nepal, Bangladesh, Brazil, Colombia and Argentina, and inaugurated a new assembly plant in Thailand (Dec 2024, 30,000-unit capacity). Market share cited at 9% in Europe, 8% in the Americas, 9% in Asia-Pacific; management focus areas include North America, Latin America, Asia-Pacific and SAARC (Bangladesh, Nepal). This reflects export/diversification momentum without an explicit 'China+1' framing.

rural.evidence: Company/analyst commentary references rural and semi-urban demand as a driver of two-wheeler volume recovery (e.g., 'increase in inquiries and showroom traffic being the primary indicator of the rural and semi-urban markets revival'), but no specific rural revenue percentage was found in available sources.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Eicher Motors is reported to be in a strong net-cash position (total debt ~INR 300 crore/₹3.0B vs. cash & short-term investments of ~INR 4,870 crore/₹48.7B), suggesting low rate sensitivity, though no floating-rate liability percentage was disclosed in sources found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Unverified secondary-source claim (search summary, not confirmed against a primary filing) that Eicher Motors was approved under the 'Champion OEM Incentive Scheme' (general vehicle category) of India's PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry. No revenue/incentive amount specific to Eicher Motors was found; a separate industry-wide figure (~INR 1,999.94 crore released in FY25 across 5 approved applicants, EV-manufacturing focused) could not be confirmed as applicable to Eicher Motors specifically.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company received export orders from the US, Europe and APAC; exports contributed ~25-30% of revenue driven by allocated markets (SAARC, Southeast Asia) and global feeder factory products; company began construction of a new manufacturing unit at Karjan, Vadodara to 'strengthen manufacturing capacity, supply chain resilience and localisation.' No explicit 'China+1' framing found in available sources.

govt_capex.evidence: Utilities (largely government-owned) historically dominated the order book (reported as ~96% of orders in a recent quarter before diversifying toward industries and transport/infra); company positioned to capitalize on India's estimated $105bn grid capex by FY32E. Precise FY24-25 revenue % from government/utility customers not found in available sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export orders received from US, Europe and APAC in USD/other foreign currencies; exports ~25-30% of revenue/order book, implying corresponding foreign-currency revenue exposure, but no explicit hedging policy disclosure found.

pli_scheme.evidence: As of the sources found, PLI for transmission/power equipment manufacturing was only being 'explored' by the Ministry of Power (per a government official's statement), not an active scheme Hitachi Energy India participates in.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Long-term debt reported down to ~Rs 67 million (FY25) from ~Rs 3,000 million (FY24), a 98% decline; no floating-vs-fixed rate breakdown found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company reported hedge losses (e.g., ~INR 164 crore for a full year, ~INR 70 crore in Q4 FY26, and ~$10-14M mark-to-market in Q1 FY27) attributed to USD/GBP/EUR forward contracts, indicating active currency hedging, but the specific FY24-25 AR hedging policy text and % of revenue in USD were not found in available sources. Revenue by geography (Americas 53.9%, EMEA 34.7%, remainder ~11.4% including India/APAC) proxies substantial foreign-currency revenue exposure.

china_plus_one.evidence: Netweb positions itself as an 'Indian origin OEM' building supercomputing, AI and data-centre systems under the 'Make in India' initiative, with CMD stating 'Indigenous server technology vital for India's security.' Company also discloses dependency on a global supply chain (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, memory, networking) and notes supply constraints/export restrictions could affect availability. No explicit 'China+1' framing tied to revenue growth found in available sources.

govt_capex.evidence: Reported customer mix: Government 42.8% vs Non-Government 57.2% (period of this disclosure not confirmed as FY24-25 specific; may reflect a more recent quarter).

inr_exposure.evidence: As a net importer of hardware components (GPUs, memory, networking equipment), Netweb is exposed to INR/USD fluctuations on the cost side; no specific hedging policy or USD revenue % disclosed in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Netweb received an incentive of ~Rs 5.93-5.94 crore under the PLI Scheme 2.0 for IT Hardware, described as its first claim under the scheme. Revenue % attributable to PLI-linked production not disclosed.

rural.evidence: Company describes continuing 'to dominate in semi-urban and rural segments with trusted value brands,' with the Country Liquor segment catering to 'the mass market, especially the price-sensitive consumer base in rural areas.' No specific revenue % attributed to rural found.

crude_exposure.evidence: AR/brokerage commentary notes 'the cost of grain, ENA, and glass has been volatile,' pressuring gross margins, offset by premiumisation and price increases. This reflects general raw-material (grain/ENA/glass/packaging) volatility rather than an explicit crude-oil-linked % disclosure.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export sales (~6.56% of turnover, to 100+ countries) imply some foreign-currency revenue exposure, but no explicit USD revenue % or hedging policy disclosure found.

govt_capex.evidence: HAL's principal customer is India's Ministry of Defence / Indian Air Force; company is a defence PSU with domestic government orders forming the overwhelming majority of revenue, though no single AR-disclosed 'govt capex %' figure was located (third-party summaries, not primary AR).

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports reported at roughly 1% of total revenue in third-party company profiles; HAL has stated an ambition to raise export share (via Dornier aircraft and helicopter sales to Africa, Middle East and South-East Asia) to ~25% of revenue over time (source: eurasiantimes.com and analyst notes, not primary AR text).

china_plus_one.evidence: CDMO segment reported ~98% overseas / ~2% domestic revenue mix; combined share of top-3 global customers (Bayer Crop Science, Corteva Agriscience, Fermion) in exports rose to 80% in H1FY26 from 63% in FY24, consistent with global agrochemical/pharma majors diversifying sourcing toward India. Specialty Chemicals + CDMO together were ~51% of total exports in H1FY26. AR/broker commentary does not use explicit 'China+1' framing, so classified moderate rather than strong (source: sell-side broker notes/analyst summaries, not primary AR text).

inr_exposure.evidence: Company has targeted USD 100mn of dedicated export revenue by FY27; quarterly export share of total revenue varied widely across FY25 (~57% in Q1FY25 to ~77% in Q4FY25 per broker reports), so no single reliable full-year AR-disclosed domestic/export % could be confirmed (source: broker/analyst reports, not primary AR).

pli_scheme.evidence: No confirmed company-specific PLI scheme approval found; only generic broker commentary referencing government 'PLI and Atmanirbhar Bharat' policy tailwinds for the chemicals sector broadly, not a documented company-specific PLI benefit.

govt_capex.evidence: EIL is a Navratna CPSE under India's Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas; oil & gas / petrochemical sector projects for PSU clients (IOCL, BPCL, HPCL, GAIL, etc.) comprised ~55% of the FY25 order book, with non-oil & gas segments (data centres, labs, academic complexes, energy transition) making up the remaining ~45% (previously ~90% oil & gas linked in earlier years) (source: psuwatch.com, third-party reporting, not primary AR).

inr_exposure.evidence: International/overseas operations revenue was reported at ~Rs 371 crore in FY25 (up 32% YoY) against standalone FY25 revenue of ~Rs 3,198 crore, implying international revenue share of roughly 11-12%; overseas presence anchored by an Abu Dhabi engineering office serving ADNOC and other Middle East/Africa/South-East Asia clients (source: psuwatch.com and business-standard summaries, not primary AR).

rural.evidence: Tier 3-and-below cities (linked to the company's rural/underserved-market push including its 'GraminFit' initiative) contributed approximately 39% of total revenue in FY25/FY26, up from 34% in FY23, a ~16.7% CAGR over the period (source: investor presentation / analyst summaries, not primary AR text).

inr_exposure.evidence: International operations (Nepal, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Saudi Arabia, Nigeria, plus a newly incorporated Dubai subsidiary) reportedly account for under 2% of total revenue (source: third-party financial/company summaries, not primary AR).

china_plus_one.evidence: Secondary/broker sources (Jefferies, industry commentary) identify Divi's Laboratories as a key beneficiary as multinational innovators diversify CDMO/API supply chains away from China; Divi's has signed long-term supply agreements with a global pharma major and is investing Rs 650-700 crore in capacity expansion. Primary AR PDF (divislabs.com) was blocked in this environment, so this is not a confirmed direct quote from the report itself.

inr_exposure.evidence: Secondary source (Quartr Q1 FY26 summary referencing FY25): exports accounted for ~88% of sales revenue.

govt_capex.evidence: Secondary source (result-update commentary on FY25/26 outlook): 'India's outlook is positive, supported by domestic demand, RBI's rate cuts, and robust infrastructure spending... railways and aviation, which are core focus areas for the government, continue to do well.' No revenue % disclosed; AR itself (aplapollo.com) was inaccessible.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Secondary source (management commentary): HRC/raw-material price changes are typically passed through to customers within 5-8 days rather than via financial hedging instruments; no explicit currency hedging policy found.
inr_exposure.evidence: Exports were ~6% of FY25 sales; company is overwhelmingly domestic-revenue focused.

rural.evidence: Secondary source (earnings commentary FY25): 'Rural markets continued to outpace urban markets in the Consumer and Bazaar segment,' with medium-term growth supported by 'rural demand outpacing urban.' No rural revenue % disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Secondary/broker sources describe Vinyl Acetate Monomer (VAM), a crude-oil derivative, as accounting for roughly 35-40% of Pidilite's raw material costs; figure not confirmed against the primary AR (pidilite.com was inaccessible in this environment).

china_plus_one.evidence: AR 'Derisking our supply chain' section: 'As we operate in an increasingly uncertain global landscape, derisking our supply chain is essential... By diversifying across both geographic locations and our supplier base, we have worked to ensure that we are not overly reliant on any single country.' This is framed as inbound raw-material sourcing risk mitigation, not an outbound China+1 export-demand opportunity; the word 'China' does not appear anywhere in the report, and standalone export contribution is only 0.30% of turnover (BRSR).

rural.evidence: AR narrative (FY25 review): 'the rural segment showed signs of recovery, supported by improved agricultural output and rising income levels... expanding opportunities in both urban and rural markets' driven by India's low per-capita paint consumption. No rural revenue % disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: AR narrative (FY25 review): 'the run-up to the General Election saw a temporary reduction in government infrastructure spending, further dampening demand.' No revenue % disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Standalone: 'The Company does not have any significant variable rate interest bearing liabilities as at March 31, 2025 and March 31, 2024.' Consolidated: 'the Group has variable rate interest bearing liabilities at March 31, 2025 and March 31, 2024, [but] there would not be any material impact on pretax profit and pre tax equity of the Group on account of any anticipated fluctuations in interest.'

crude_exposure.evidence: Per company's commodity materiality policy disclosed in AR: 'No commodity is considered to be material' for commodity price risk/hedging disclosure purposes; no crude-linked (TiO2/resin) raw material % given.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: AR: 'The Company's Foreign Exchange exposure with respect to payables and loans are managed by continuously monitoring the exchange rates and premiums for forward cover and such exposure is hedged on a short-term basis when commercially expedient to do so.' Company/Group 'uses forward currency contracts to hedge its foreign currency risks,' mainly payables, not designated as formal Ind AS 109 hedge relationships.
inr_exposure.evidence: Consolidated FY25 segment note: Revenue Within India Rs 10,610.15 cr, Outside India Rs 847.33 cr, Total Rs 11,457.48 cr (Outside India = 7.4% of consolidated revenue).

china_plus_one.evidence: Company's export footprint spans the United States, Japan, United Kingdom and China; in FY25 it supplied 250+ different components to Jaguar Land Rover's overseas facilities in Austria, Slovakia and the UK as a single-source supplier, and has pursued diversification into defense/aerospace supply chains (Israeli and Indian defence OEMs, a Plasan partnership, facilities acquired outside India for aircraft/space and combat-aircraft OEM manufacturing). No explicit 'China+1' framing or revenue attribution to it was found in available sources.

crude_exposure.evidence: Raw material costs (sheet metal, steel wire, polymers) were reported at 65.33% of total expenses in FY24 and 63.73% in Q1FY25; primarily metal-based, with partial crude-linked exposure via polymer inputs, but no explicit crude-oil raw-material percentage of revenue was disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports to US, Japan, UK and China exist alongside the JLR overseas supply relationship, implying some foreign-currency revenue, but no USD revenue % or hedging policy was found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Third-party commentary suggests Belrise is 'positioned to benefit' from auto-sector PLI incentives, but no confirmed AR/company disclosure of actual PLI scheme participation or revenue benefit was found.

rural.evidence: Company is strengthening a pan-India distribution network (800+ distributors, 5,000 channel partners, ~2,15,000 retailers, targeting 2,50,000) with a stated focus on Tier 2/3 cities and rural areas; rural electrification schemes cited as a demand driver for cables. No rural revenue % disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Demand cited as supported by power transmission & distribution, railways, telecom, renewable energy and industrial capex; center/state government capex up ~3x/1.7x over FY19-24 cited as a past demand driver, with DISCOM capex under the revamped distribution sector scheme also cited. A Rs.500-crore capex program (incl. new e-beam facility for solar/railway cables) was underway through FY25. No specific govt-capex-linked revenue % disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Copper is the dominant raw material (external estimates put copper near 70-75% of cable manufacturing cost); PVC (a petrochemical/oil derivative) is also used. No company-disclosed crude-oil-linked raw material percentage of revenue was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports are a small part of the business (e.g., ~Rs 50 crore in a single recent quarter versus consolidated FY25 sales of Rs 5,318.89 crore), concentrated in high-margin optical fiber cable sales to the US and Europe. No USD revenue % or hedging policy disclosure found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Communication cables (including optical fiber) were roughly 9-10% of sales, and optic fiber cable volumes grew strongly (~52.5% YoY cited); the segment is eligible under India's Telecom PLI scheme and the company is expanding OFC/glass-preform manufacturing capacity. However, no confirmed disclosure of actual PLI scheme enrollment or incentive revenue was found.
No PLI scheme applicable to the Indian alcobev/spirits sector was found; no disclosure of PLI participation.

govt_capex.evidence: India's airport infrastructure capex is projected to exceed Rs 1 lakh crore over the next five years, with airport count projected to grow from 163 (FY25) to 350-400 by FY47; this AAI/government-driven airport expansion is cited as a structural growth driver for TFS's airport-based Travel QSR and lounge business. No specific revenue percentage tied to government capex was disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: TFS operates Travel QSR outlets and lounges in Malaysia (29 QSR outlets) and entered Hong Kong in FY25 (1 lounge), alongside its dominant India operations (413 QSR outlets, 28 lounges), implying some foreign-currency revenue exposure, but no USD/foreign revenue % or hedging policy was disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme applicable to travel retail/F&B services was found; no disclosure of PLI participation.
